problem:
A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(\sqrt{3}k,-k),$ where $k$ is a positive real number. Find the polar coordinates of $P$ expressed in terms of $k.$ Give the polar angle in radians and do not round the answer.

Expressed in terms of $k,$ the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{3}k)^{2}+(-k)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3{k}^{2}+{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{k}^{2}} \\  & =2k\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-k}{\sqrt{3}k})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})| \\  & =|-\frac{\pi }{6}| \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point lies in the fourth quadrant, we subtract the reference angle from $2\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{11\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are $(2k,\frac{11\pi }{6}).$
